title: Salesforce MCP Server: Every Endpoint, Tool, and What AI Agents Can Do
summary: A complete map of Salesforce's hosted MCP servers: the four SObject endpoints, every tool they expose, product servers, custom tools, and what an AI agent can…
body_markdown:
## What does the Salesforce MCP server cover?


**Short answer:** Salesforce's hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets an AI client such as Claude or ChatGPT work with your org through a fixed set of servers. Four SObject servers handle CRM records:` sobject-reads` (query and search),` sobject-mutations` (create and update),` sobject-deletes` (delete), and` sobject-all` (everything). Product servers add Data 360, Tableau Next, CRM Analytics, CMS content, and Setup. Admins can also publish Flows, Apex, and catalog APIs as custom tools. Every call runs under the connected user's permissions and sharing rules.


*Last verified against Salesforce's Hosted MCP Servers documentation on October 23, 2026.*


## What is the Salesforce MCP server?


MCP is an open protocol that lets an AI model call tools in another system. Salesforce hosts its own MCP servers, so you don't run or maintain anything. You point an MCP client at a server URL, sign in with OAuth, and the model can read schema, query records, and make changes.


Three facts shape how you use it:


- 01


**Admins enable each server.** Standard servers ship disabled. An admin turns on the ones the org needs.


- 02


**Salesforce fixes the tool sets.** You can't add or remove tools on a standard server. To control what an agent can do, you pick a narrower server.


- 03


**Salesforce security applies to every call.** Field-level security, object permissions, and sharing rules gate each tool. An agent can't edit a field the user can't edit in Lightning.


## What endpoints does Salesforce MCP cover?


All SObject servers share one base URL.


Pick the narrowest SObject server that does the job


-


Production:` https://api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp/v1/platform/<server>`


-


Sandbox and scratch orgs:` https://api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp/v1/sandbox/platform/<server>`


Server Endpoint suffix Operations Pick it when


SObject Reads` platform/sobject-reads` Schema, SOQL, search, relationships. No writes. You want analysis, pipeline reviews, or account research with zero write risk


SObject Mutations` platform/sobject-mutations` Create and update. No delete. Agents log tasks, update stages, or create leads


SObject Deletes` platform/sobject-deletes` Delete only You run a supervised cleanup job


SObject All` platform/sobject-all` Full CRUD plus query, search, relationship traversal A trusted user wants full productivity and you rely on their permissions as the guardrail


All four servers cover standard and custom objects.


## Which tools does the SObject All server expose?


` sobject-all` holds the full tool set. The narrower servers expose subsets of it.


Tool What it does Notes


` getObjectSchema` Returns a compact index of business objects, or full field detail for one object Includes admin-written guidance, such as "use` Calculated_ACV__c` instead of` Amount` "


` soqlQuery` Runs a SOQL query Supports parent lookups and child subqueries. Caps at 50,000 records per transaction


` find` Runs a SOSL text search across objects Returns up to 2,000 records. Use it when you don't know which object holds the data


` getUserInfo` Returns the signed-in user's ID, role, profile, manager, and timezone Lets the agent resolve "my accounts"


` listRecentSobjectRecords` Lists records the user viewed or changed recently Resolves "that opportunity I was looking at"


` getRelatedRecords` Walks a relationship from a parent record Example: every Contact on an Account


` createSobjectRecord` Creates a record Fails on missing required fields or validation rules


` updateSobjectRecord` Updates fields on a record by ID Leaves omitted fields unchanged


` updateRelatedRecord` Updates a parent record through a child-to-parent path Works up to five levels deep


Delete tool Deletes a record Available on` sobject-all` and` sobject-deletes` only


## What can you do with it? Example prompts by server


Salesforce's own examples show the range:


One agent request: two successful calls, two HPIs once metering starts


-


**Reads:** "Show me all open opportunities in the Manufacturing industry over $500K, grouped by owner."


-


**Reads:** "Find every Contact associated with Acme Corp and return their names, titles, and email addresses."


-


**Mutations:** "Create a follow-up task for every Account where the last activity date is more than 90 days ago."


-


**Mutations:** "Update the Stage on opportunity Acme Renewal to Closed Won and set the Close Date to today."


A realistic sales request chains several tools. "Find opportunities over $30K with no recent activity, summarize the account, and create follow-up tasks" runs a SOQL query, walks to related contacts and activities, then creates one task per opportunity. Count those calls. Under Salesforce's new billing model, each successful call from a registered agent will consume Flex Credits. Our[Salesforce MCP pricing guide](https://www.stacksync.com/blog/salesforce-mcp-pricing-flex-credits-hpi) explains the meter.


## What else does Salesforce MCP cover beyond CRM records?


### Product-specific servers


Server Coverage Status


Data 360 Query unified customer data with SQL Available


Tableau Next (` analytics/tableau-next` ) Semantic models, KPIs, dashboard metadata, natural-language analytics Available


CRM Analytics Apps, dataset schemas, SAQL queries, dashboard and lens metadata. Read-only Beta, sandbox and scratch orgs only


Content Read-Only / Content Write Salesforce CMS workspaces, channels, content, folders Available


Headless 360 Setup and platform capabilities through Discover, Describe, and Dispatch tools, plus Archive Connect Beta


Metadata Grounding Discover objects, fields, LWCs, flows, Apex classes, permission sets Beta


### Custom tools you publish


Admins and developers can expose existing logic as MCP tools without new integration code:


-


**Flows** built in Flow Builder


-


**Apex invocable actions** (` @InvocableMethod` )


-


**` @AuraEnabled` Apex methods** that already back Lightning components


-


**Apex REST endpoints** (` @RestResource` )


-


**APIs registered in the API Catalog** , including standard platform APIs and a subset of Connect APIs


-


**Prompt Builder templates** , surfaced as MCP prompts where the client supports them


This is where the hosted MCP stops being a generic CRUD layer. If your org already runs a "Create Renewal Opportunity" flow with validation and approvals, the agent can call that flow instead of writing records field by field.


### Salesforce DX MCP is a separate thing


Salesforce also ships a DX MCP server for developers. It retrieves and deploys metadata, runs Apex tests, manages scratch orgs, and assigns permission sets. Salesforce has announced that the DX MCP server reaches end of life on November 2, 2026. Use the hosted servers above for business data. Our[self-hosted vs hosted guide](https://www.stacksync.com/blog/self-hosted-vs-hosted-salesforce-mcp) covers the move.
